messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Paging oncall: unusual KV cache growth and continuous-batching throughput drop in us-west-2. Observed pack-shed and short-request starvation. Incident link: https://redwood/inci/1719876543
oncall_sre_amy: Acked. -amy. Pulling metrics now.
alice_eng: I see a big spike in kv_mem_resident and a simultaneous drop in short-request throughput (p50 p95 increasing). Graphs: https://dash/kv/cache/growth
bob_infra: Logs show a surge of prefetch jobs and repeated cache-ejects. Possibly prefetch loop bug from yesterday's rollout.
oncall_sre_amy: Paging @kiran_englead and @pm_james for impact assessment. Repeating: customers seeing higher tail latencies and increased 429s for short chats.
kiran_englead: I'm in. Can we throttle prefetch and reduce pack size? Suggest disable prefetch flag and set max_batch_tokens=256 for affected pools.
alice_eng: Agreed. Quick mitigation: set prefetch_enabled=false on pool kv-usw2-prod and lower max_batch_tokens.
observability-bot: metric alert: kv_cache_rss > 80% for 6m; batch_queue_delay p99 > 800ms for short requests.
oncall_sre_amy: Running emergency change: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/batch-scheduler PRELOAD_PREFETCH=false --context=prod-usw2
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/batch-scheduler MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=256 --context=prod-usw2
```
Executing now.
alice_eng: Also rolling back commit 9a7f3e2 from yesterday that introduced aggressive prefetch heuristics.
bob_infra: Rolling back via canary then full. kubectl rollout undo deployment/prefetcher --to-revision=12
oncall_sre_amy: Changes applied. Monitoring... please watch p50/p95 for short requests and kv eviction rate.
observability-bot: post-change: kv_cache_rss down 12% within 2m; batch_queue_delay p99 improved to ~220ms.
pm_james: Customer impact: 3 enterprise customers reported noticeable latency increases (tickets #3245, #3246, #3250). We're telling them mitigation in progress.
kiran_englead: Create postmortem placeholder and assign owners. I'll own code rollback. Amy, please collect timeline and escalation notes for SRE handoff.
oncall_sre_amy: Timeline notes added to incident doc: https://redwood/incidents/1719876543/doc
alice_eng: Running loadgen on canary to validate throughput under mixed long/short workload. Quick config tweak: enable fairness heuristic backoff to 0.5 for 5m.
bob_infra: Deployed fairness backoff. Command:
```
redwoodctl config set scheduler.fairness.backoff 0.5 --pool kv-usw2-prod
```
observability-bot: After fairness backoff p99 short-latency returned to baseline ~95ms, long tail persists slightly for heavy batches.
oncall_sre_amy: Ok team — we'll keep this incident open for 1hr to verify stability. If no regression, plan a controlled rollback of prefetch heuristics to stable branch and add additional tests.
pm_james: Communicated to customers: "We identified and mitigated an internal cache prefetch surge that increased tail latency. We're monitoring and will follow up with a root cause timeline." :thumbsup: 
kiran_englead: Next actions: add unit tests for prefetch loop, rate-limit prefetch jobs, add per-tenant KV prefetch cap. I can get PR out within today.
oncall_sre_amy: Handoff to evening on-call @oncall_sre_ben at 1719878200. Ben, please watch the metrics and be ready to re-enable prefetch if needed with config guardrails.
oncall_sre_amy: Handing over. Summary: surge caused cache blowup -> continuous-batching starvation for short requests -> mitigated by disabling prefetch, reducing max_batch_tokens, enabling fairness backoff. Customer impact limited to elevated latencies and a few 429s; tickets opened.
oncall_sre_amy: Closing shout: :white_check_mark: mitigation deployed, monitoring stable. Will file full incident after stabilization.
oncall_sre_ben: Acked. Taking over. -ben
